responsibility: Defines the Rust backend’s central compilation context, the state carrier used while lowering resolved HIR and TyTy types into GCC trees and backend variables. It owns caches for compiled types, functions, closures, constants, labels, variables, pattern bindings, and monomorphized instances; tracks nested scopes, statements, functions, loops, constant-evaluation contexts, and closure captures; exposes resolver, type-check, mapping, mangling, and backend services; and finally collects the generated global definitions to emit to the GCC backend.
same_name_distinction: Defines the Context class itself: the central backend state object with caches, stacks, declaration maps, monomorphization tables, loop/const tracking, and backend/resolver accessors. Unlike the .cc file, it primarily specifies the context’s stored state and broad API surface rather than the concrete initialization, hashing, and closure-binding logic.
